# Saṅkhapālacariya (Cp 20)

**ID:** Cp 20
**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Saṅkhapālacariya
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0512m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅkhapālacariya* (Cp 20) is the twentieth narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, the canonical collection of verse accounts illustrating the Bodhisatta's cultivation of the perfections (*pāramitā*) [Bareau]. In this birth, the Bodhisatta is reborn as Saṅkhapāla, a king of serpents endowed with extraordinary potency, fearful venom, fangs, and a forked tongue [Bareau]. Resolutely determining upon his ascetic observance along the crossroads of a great highway, he undertakes his vows without regard for his own life, illustrating resolve formulated around the "four factors" (*caturo aṅge adhiṭṭhāya*) [Bareau; Lim 2009].
